title.name: The Green Men
title.subtitle: A mine through time
title.players: One miner, one mine through time
menu.easy.note: Bumps and bad air do less harm.
menu.normal.note: No clock: take your time. Fill the museum and reach the cave at the bottom.
intro.1: Under Navarre lie mines from many ages. The deeper you dig, the further back in time you go.
intro.2: At the top, the 20th-century potash mine. Further down, the kings' iron, medieval copper and Roman galleries.
intro.3: And at the very bottom, the cave of the Green Men, the oldest miners of all. On the way, old things wait to be found for the village museum.
howto.title: How to play
howto.walk: Stick ← →: walk. Push into rock to dig
howto.dig: Stick ↓: dig down. You leave ladders behind you
howto.ladders: Stick ↑: climb (a ladder goes in if there is none, and you can dig up). [B] puts a ladder in
howto.light: Your light burns down underground: refill it at the lamp room. Ore sells at the weighbridge
howto.sell: Ore sells itself at the weighbridge
howto.shop: [A] at the workshop: tools, cage stations in the old shaft, and things for your belt
howto.danger: Dangers warn you: bad air hisses, loose rock creaks, water drips. With water over your head, your breath runs out. If your light or strength runs out, your workmates bring you up
help.play: ← → walk · ↓ dig · ↑ climb · [B] ladder · [A] belt · [C] use

call.air: Bad air! Get out of it
call.rescue: Your workmates brought you up: −{cost}. The ore stayed below
call.lowLight: Your light is running low! Head up
call.lowHealth: You're worn out: go up and rest

gl.title: Underground
gl.potasas.name: Potash of Navarre
gl.potasas.text: Here at Beriáin, potash was mined from 1963 to 1986. It was hard work, and it brought a whole mining town to life.
gl.potasa.name: Potash
gl.potasa.text: Reddish potassium salts. They make fertiliser that helps farm crops grow.
gl.hierro.name: Iron for the king
gl.hierro.text: At Eugi and Orbaizeta, iron from the hills was smelted with charcoal from the forests. Royal arms factories stood there.
gl.magnesita.name: Magnesite
gl.magnesita.text: A rock that stands enormous heat. It was found in the 1940s, when someone spotted pieces of it in the river Arga.
gl.cobre.name: The copper of the Arce valley
gl.cobre.text: Almost 700 years ago, the kings of Navarre looked for copper and silver in the Arce valley. They brought experts from far away, like Braccio from Florence.
gl.plata.name: Silver
gl.plata.text: Silver was made into coins. That is why kings wanted to know where to find it.
gl.romanos.name: Roman galleries
gl.romanos.text: About 2,000 years ago, the Romans cut galleries into the northern hills for silver and lead. Many of the people who worked there were not free.
gl.galena.name: Galena
gl.galena.text: It shines like metal. Lead and silver were made from it.
gl.bronce.name: Bronze Age miners
gl.bronce.text: Thousands of years ago, people here broke the rock with fire and stone hammers to get copper. Their tools were made of stone and bone.
gl.malaquita.name: Malachite
gl.malaquita.text: A green stone, green because it holds copper. The first miners looked for it by its colour.
gl.air.name: Bad air
gl.air.text: Underground, the air is sometimes not good to breathe. Miners learned to let fresh air into the tunnels.
gl.loose.name: Loose rock
gl.loose.text: Dig under loose rock and it falls. That is why miners propped up their tunnels with timber.
gl.escalera.name: Ladders
gl.escalera.text: The first miners climbed notched tree trunks. Wooden ladders came later.
gl.torno.name: The windlass
gl.torno.text: A wheel and rope over the shaft: it hauled up miners and ore much faster.
gl.jaula.name: The cage
gl.jaula.text: A lift for miners. In mines like the potash pits, it went down very deep at every shift.
gl.companeros.name: Workmates
gl.companeros.text: Miners looked after each other: if someone's light went out, the others went down to fetch them.
cave.1: You have reached the cave of the Green Men. Thousands of years ago it was a copper mine, and later the place where 35 people were laid to rest.
cave.2: In 1958, at Urbiola, their bones were found, stained green by the copper in the rock. That is why they are called the Green Men. Some are thought to have been metal seekers.
cave.3: Their work was hard, like that of every miner who came after them. Thanks to them there were tools, coins and fertiliser. Today we remember them.
up.pick.0.name: Hammer and fire
up.pick.1.name: Iron pick
up.pick.1.text: Digs faster and breaks harder rock
up.pick.2.name: Drill and powder
up.pick.2.text: Blasters bored holes and filled them with powder
up.pick.3.name: Pneumatic hammer
up.pick.3.text: Driven by compressed air: breaks any rock
up.lamp.0.name: Torch
up.lamp.1.name: Oil lamp
up.lamp.2.name: Carbide lamp
up.lamp.3.name: Electric cap lamp
up.lamp.3.text: On the helmet: brighter, and lasts a long time

up.bag.2.name: Leather pack
up.bag.3.name: Mine cart

up.gear.1.name: Leather helmet
up.gear.2.name: Helmet and boots
up.gear.3.name: Steel helmet

up.ladders.1.name: Wooden ladders
up.ladders.2.name: Light ladders

final.title: Your mining career
fact.beriain: Beriáin was a village of 254 people. With the potash mine, from 1963, it became a mining town.
fact.encierro: In 1975 the potash miners stayed down the mine to ask for better conditions, and many people in Navarre joined them.
fact.arga: Eugi's magnesite was found in the 1940s, when someone spotted pieces of it in the river Arga.
fact.dolomita: The Eugi mine is famous around the world for its dolomite crystals, now kept in museums.
fact.milan: It is said that Philip II brought armourers from Milan to Eugi to make helmets and armour.
fact.orbaizeta: The Orbaizeta arms factory was founded in 1784, on the site of an ironworks from 1432.
fact.braccio: In 1362 a Florentine called Braccio ran the copper mine in the Arce valley.
fact.aia: About 2,000 years ago the Romans cut galleries by the Peñas de Aia, near Lesaka, for silver and lead.
fact.urbiola: The cave of the Green Men was found in 1958 at Urbiola, near Estella.
fact.ninos: For centuries children worked in mines too, carrying ore. Today the law forbids it.
fact.lampisteria: Mines had a lamp room, where the miners' lamps were looked after and handed out.
final.sub: You have dug down through thousands of years of Navarre's mines.
fact.plantilla: At the end of 1974, 2,200 people worked at Potasas de Navarra.
fact.sellado: The potash galleries, all joined to each other, were sealed in the early 1990s.
fact.europa: Today more than half of Navarre's magnesite is sold to other European countries.
fact.eugipueblo: The Eugi factory was like a town: about 700 people, with a school, a doctor and a chapel.
fact.convencion: French soldiers destroyed the Eugi factory in 1794, in the War of the Convention.
fact.ruinas: The Orbaizeta factory closed in 1884. Its ruins still stand in the woods by the Irati forest.
fact.blanca: In 1432 Queen Blanca of Navarre allowed the iron, silver and lead of the Aezkoa valley to be worked.
fact.girardi: In 1340 a report said Navarre's copper and silver mines lay by Gipuzkoa and in the Arce valley.
fact.betelu: In the 16th and 17th centuries mines opened at Betelu, Imízcoz and Urrobi, mostly for iron.
fact.gorramendi: On Gorramendi, in Baztan, traces remain of how the Romans searched for gold.
fact.arditurri: The Roman galleries by the Peñas de Aia were worked from Roman times until the late 20th century.
fact.azurita: At the Urbiola cave, malachite and azurite were dug out: green and blue copper minerals.

call.deep: Deep water: your light burns faster

item.dynamite.name: Dynamite
item.dynamite.text: Short fuse. Breaks 3×3, even rock one grade harder than your tool. Get clear!
item.kit.name: First-aid kit
item.kit.text: Gives you back a good part of your strength
item.oil.name: Oil flask
item.rope.name: Winch rope
item.rope.text: Hauls you up in a few seconds to the nearest station or the surface, load and all
museum.title: The village museum
museum.new: A new piece for the museum!
choice.title: You reached the cave
choice.text: You can keep digging to fill the museum. When you are ready, take the piece at the back of the cave and get out fast.
choice.end: [B] end your career here, without the piece
final.cave: The cave of the Green Men
gl.agua.name: Water
gl.agua.text: Deep mines fill with water. Miners got it out with pumps, wheels or drainage tunnels.
gl.dinamita.name: Dynamite
gl.dinamita.text: Blasters put it in holes drilled in the rock. Before lighting it, they warned everyone to get clear.
gl.museo.name: The museum
gl.museo.text: The things miners left behind tell us how they lived and worked. That is why museums keep them with care.
find.casco.name: A miner's helmet
find.casco.text: A helmet from the potash mine. Every shift, miners went down wearing one, with a lamp on the front.
find.ficha.name: A lamp token
find.ficha.text: In many mines, each miner swapped a numbered token for a lamp. A token left over showed who was still down below.
find.carburo.name: A carbide lamp
find.carburo.text: Water dripped onto carbide and made a gas that burned with a bright white flame. Many miners used these lamps.
find.bala.name: A cannonball
find.bala.text: The royal factories of Eugi and Orbaizeta made ammunition for the king's army from the iron of these hills.
find.herradura.name: A horseshoe
find.herradura.text: Mules and horses carried iron and charcoal along the mountain paths. A lost horseshoe is a common find.
find.coraza.name: A piece of armour
find.coraza.text: It is said that Philip II brought armourers from Milan to Eugi to make helmets and armour.
find.dinero.name: A medieval coin
find.dinero.text: The kings of Navarre made coins of silver. That is why the mines mattered so much to them.
find.candil.name: An oil lamp
find.candil.text: An iron oil lamp with a hook, to hang on the rock. Its little flame lit the work.
find.crisol.name: A crucible
find.crisol.text: A clay pot for melting metal. Crucibles were used to test how much copper or silver the ore held.
find.moneda.name: A Roman coin
find.moneda.text: Silver from mines like these ended up as coins like this one.
find.lucerna.name: A Roman lamp
find.lucerna.text: A little clay oil lamp. The Romans lit their galleries with lamps like this one.
find.pico.name: A Roman pick
find.pico.text: The iron head of a pick. Roman galleries were cut by hand, one blow at a time.
find.hacha.name: A bronze axe
find.hacha.text: Copper and tin melted together make bronze. The metal from the mines became tools like this one.
find.ceramica.name: A pottery sherd
find.ceramica.text: A piece of a handmade clay pot. Pots like this held food and water.
find.martillo.name: A stone hammer
find.martillo.text: A round stone with a groove for a handle. The first miners are thought to have broken rock with hammers like this.
item.bellows.name: Bellows
item.bellows.text: Pushes the bad air out of the stretch of tunnel you are in
ben.lampAir: warns of bad air {n} m away
call.fizzle: The flame flares and the fuse goes out! Never fire near bad air
call.under: Head under water! Hold your breath and get out
call.noBreath: Out of breath! Get out of the water
call.vented: The air is moving: the bad air drifts out
call.crown: [A] take the piece (the old mine will wake!)
gl.llama.name: Fire and bad air
gl.llama.text: Some bad air in mines can catch fire. That is why miners never brought a flame or a fuse near bad air.
gl.ventilacion.name: Ventilation
gl.ventilacion.text: If a tunnel has two ways out, air flows through it and carries the bad air away. A dead end keeps it much longer.
find.collar.name: A necklace of green beads
find.collar.text: Green stone beads on a thread. People of the Bronze Age are thought to have worn ornaments like this.
crown.kicker: At the back of the cave
crown.text: Something shines at the back of the cave: the piece the museum has waited for all your career. When you take it, the old mine will wake and water will rise from below: you will have to get out fast, by the ladders, tunnels and cages you have built.
crown.ready: Get ready first: a full lamp, ladders, perhaps a rope. You can fetch more pieces before.
esc.rumble: The old mine is waking up!
esc.rising: The water is rising! Climb your ladders to the cage
esc.escaped: Safe! The cage takes you up with the piece
esc.caught: The cage lifts you out of the water! The piece comes with you
fin.title: The mining museum opens
fin.sub.escaped: A miner climbs out of the old mine with a Bronze Age necklace, ahead of the water
fin.head.caught: Find at Urbiola, and a rescue!
fin.sub.caught: The cage lifts a miner and a great find out of the water. Everyone safe and sound
fin.head.none: The village opens its mining museum
fin.sub.none: {n} pieces tell thousands of years of Navarre's mines
fin.missing: {n} pieces still to find: come back for them!
